# ens.diamonds

> ens.diamonds lets a group pool ETH into a shared vault to buy premium ENS names together. Funds sit in an audited escrow contract with unilateral refunds; purchased names are registered to a Safe multisig that all contributors control. Solo purchases are supported too.

## How it works

- When a .eth name expires and passes its 90-day grace period, ENS runs a 21-day Dutch auction (the "temporary premium"): the price starts near $100M and halves daily to $0 on day 21, on top of the standard yearly fee.
- ens.diamonds lists every name currently in that premium window with live onchain prices (https://www.ens.diamonds/).
- Anyone can create a vault for a name, set a target, and invite contributors. Deposits go to the escrow contract, never to a person.
- Contributors can withdraw their full deposit at any time while a vault is funding. Expired vaults refund everyone.
- When funded, the group moves funds to a freshly deployed Safe multisig and registers the name directly to it. Ownership shares are recorded onchain by contribution.

## Key pages

- https://www.ens.diamonds/ : live list of ENS names in their premium auction
- https://www.ens.diamonds/name/{label} : live price, decay curve, and buy/pool actions for any .eth name
- https://www.ens.diamonds/vaults : all open vaults
- https://www.ens.diamonds/faq : frequently asked questions
- https://www.ens.diamonds/about : what ens.diamonds is

## Facts

- Escrow: EnsDiamondsEscrow v2 at 0x7A11F2071344ADA4D6e53D8D8F18E83C7b03e044 (Ethereum mainnet), source verified on Etherscan, externally audited.
- Custody after purchase: Safe multisig controlled by the vault's contributors. No admin keys over user funds.
- Fees: none from ens.diamonds. Users pay the ENS price plus gas.
- Built by the Namespace team (https://namespace.ninja). Interface licensed MIT.
- A Sepolia testnet deployment exists for testing with free names.
